title: Diffraction grating; Thin-film interference
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W09-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W09-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W15-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; W15-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W09-1#N.4b, W15-1#N.6, W09-1#N.6, W15-1#N.10, W09-1#N.10, W15-1#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Slit spacing
items.clue: Symbol d: one divided by the number of lines per unit length of the plate.

items.label: Zero order
items.clue: Straight-through beam, white for white light because every λ has θ = 0 there.

items.label: Antireflection coating
items.clue: Quarter-wavelength layer on a lens, with index between those of air and glass.

items.label: Phase change
items.clue: 180° flip of a wave reflecting off a medium of greater n; absent on reflecting off a smaller n.

questions.stem: Light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating that has 800 lines per millimeter. At what angle from the normal is the second-order maximum?

A soap film (n = 1.33) in air is 115 nm thick. Light strikes it at normal incidence. What is the longest wavelength, measured in air, for which the light reflected from the film's two surfaces interferes constructively?

options.text: 306 nm
460 nm
346 nm
612 nm

questions.stem: Predict first. Monochromatic light is incident normally first on a double slit and then on a diffraction grating whose adjacent slits have the same separation d as the double slit. Every slit is equally illuminated. Compared with the double-slit fringes, how do the grating's principal maxima appear?

options.text: Farther apart than the fringes, because the grating has many more slits
At the same angles, but wider and dimmer, as the light is shared among more slits
Identical in position, width and brightness, because only d and λ matter
At the same angles as the double-slit fringes, but much sharper and brighter

questions.stem: A camera lens has an antireflection coating designed for green light, so much less green light is reflected from it than from an uncoated lens. What happens to the energy of the green light that is no longer reflected?

options.text: It is destroyed where the two reflected waves interfere destructively.
It is absorbed by the coating, which warms up slightly as a result.
It is scattered off to the sides, so it does not come back to the viewer.
It is transmitted into the lens, so more green light reaches the camera's sensor.

questions.stem: A laser beam is directed normally at a grating with 500 lines per mm. On a screen 1.00 m from the grating, the two second-order spots are 1.50 m apart. What is the wavelength of the laser light?

options.text: 750 nm
600 nm
832 nm

questions.stem: A soap film (n = 1.33) in air is lit at normal incidence by green light of wavelength 532 nm in air. Two regions of the film have thicknesses of 100 nm and 200 nm. Which comparison of the light reflected from the two regions, with its reasoning, is correct?

options.text: Brighter at 100 nm, where the film has less pigment to absorb the green
Brighter at 200 nm, where the path difference is one wavelength in the film
Brighter at 200 nm, where the thicker film reflects more of the light
Brighter at 100 nm, where the two reflected waves arrive in phase
